title: FRL Wrist Control: Wrist Movement Decoding from Surface Electromyography
description: This dataset comprises wrist-based surface electromyography (sEMG) recordings from 100 participants performing continuous cursor control via wrist flexion/extension movements. Synchronized motion capture provides ground-truth wrist angles, enabling investigation of sEMG's capacity to decode motor intent and support gesture-free human-computer interaction. The study demonstrates predictive decoding of wrist kinematics from non-invasive sEMG signals recorded at 2000 Hz using a 16-channel wristband device.
methods_description: Participants wore a 16-channel sEMG-RD wristband on their dominant wrist while performing a target acquisition task involving continuous horizontal cursor control via wrist flexion/extension. Motion capture tracked wrist angles in real-time as ground truth. Signals were recorded at 2000 Hz using bipolar differential referencing. Data underwent post-processing to address duplicate timestamps and irregular sampling, followed by resampling to regular 2000 Hz.
